tools.description: Propose creating one new room from a wall-centerline polygon. This is the only tool that accepts raw coordinates: [x,z] vertex pairs in meters, 3-32 points, simple outline. The server snaps vertices to the 0.1 m grid, normalizes winding and validates shape/minimum area; failures return refusals so you can self-correct. Call query_scene first and keep the new outline clear of existing rooms. One call proposes one room, shown as a dashed ghost until the user confirms it.
tools.name: add_room

parameters.description:

tools.description: Generate custom furniture with exact dimensions and propose placing it. Use this only when no catalog kind fits: search_catalog first. Families: bookshelf (shelves, glass doors), wardrobe (hinged/sliding), tv_stand (drawers, open shelf), desk_l (L-shaped with return), counter_run (kitchen run with sink/cooktop), scale (proportionally resize an existing kindId, factors 0.6-1.4), primitives (compose 1-24 axis-aligned boxes into a simple object no curated family covers, e.g. a drying rack or shoe rack). The server compiles a GLB, registers it in the scene library and shows the result as a ghost until the user confirms. Generated assets stay reusable through search_catalog afterwards.
tools.name: model_item

parameters.description:
Generate a custom parametric item and propose placing it.

Unlike ``add_item`` this accepts a *spec* rather than a ``kindId``: the
server compiles it to a GLB, registers it in the scene library and then
runs the usual semantic placement and validation.

oneOf.description:
Compose a simple orthogonal object from boxes.

The long-tail escape hatch: use it for shapes no curated family covers
(a drying rack, shoe rack, plant stand, partition), not for upholstered or
curved furniture. The overall footprint is measured from the parts, so the
model never has to declare a size it cannot guarantee.

category.description: Closest catalog category. Drives placement rules: storage/table/bed count as circulation blockers, decor/other do not.

items.description:
One axis-aligned box in item-local metres.

``position`` is the part centre; ``y = 0`` is the floor plane, so a
1.6 m leg standing on the floor is ``size [0.04, 1.6, 0.04]`` at
``position [x, 0.8, z]``.

tools.description: Solve a whole room at once from a furniture list and optional constraints (for example bed facing south, wardrobe, nightstand). Returns one proposal with every placement as a ghost. Use this for requests like '布置好卧室' instead of adding items one by one. Existing furniture stays as obstacles unless options.replaceExisting is true.
tools.name: auto_layout

items.description: One furniture request for a whole-room solve.

anyOf.description: Preserved agent intent so placements stay explainable and re-solvable.
anyOf.title: ItemConstraint

constraint.description: Optional intent such as facing='south', anchor.wallLabel, near or group. The solver resolves it to coordinates.

items.title: AutoLayoutItemInput

tools.description: Run structured layout checks and return every issue (collision, door/window clearance, walkway, design warnings) without changing the scene. Set visual=true when the user asks to visually inspect or check the layout; the server then captures labelled top-view screenshots, asks the VLM, rechecks issues geometrically and may propose a local re-layout.
tools.name: verify_layout

roomId.description: Limit the geometric checks to one room; omit to verify every room.
roomId.title: Roomid

visual.description: Run the VLM screenshot review closed loop when geometry passes. Set true when the user asks to visually check the layout.
visual.title: Visual

tools.description: Ask the user a clarifying question and pause the turn until they answer. Use sparingly; prefer reasonable defaults when the intent is clear.
